verifier_infrastructure_findings: The dry-run manifest test pinned a literal file digest of the append-only production verification ledger, which made any legitimate verified item break the test. The pin is now structural: the ledger's self-describing content hash and chain are asserted instead.

The safe-resume test pinned a literal CURRENT_REPOSITORY_HEAD digest, which made every commit break the test. It now asserts that the reported head is the real head and still descends from the frozen historical baseline.

build_evidence_index mis-slots provenance for two layers: the readiness layer places a document title in the organization field and a retrieval date in date_or_version, and the holdout layer places a document title in date_or_version. Underlying source rows carry correct organizations, URLs and retrieval dates, so no citation is fabricated, but package-level canadian_source_refs display the wrong field contents. Repair belongs to an infrastructure session, not to a verifier.
The package field canadian_source_refs also carries correctly attributed non-Canadian sources, notably ACC/AHA and ACG for QPILOT-V1-MED-01. The field name overstates what it holds.

Verifier artifacts must not carry an 'evidence' token in their filename under research/qgen, because the feature-evidence reuse baseline rglobs that token and would count verification records as evidence supply.
verifier_item_observations: QPILOT-V1-OBGYN-01 and QPILOT-V1-MED-02 present their key as the longest and most comprehensive option, which a test-wise candidate could exploit without clinical reasoning. Both retain genuine discriminations and all distractors are independently defeated, so this is recorded as a construction observation rather than a defect.

QPILOT-V1-SURG-01 rests on a claim recorded one level more abstractly ('CT-based assessment') than its option set requires, since CT angiography is also CT-based. The discrimination is sound and the source locator names the correct head-trauma section, but a future authoring wave should record the non-contrast discrimination as its own fact.

QPILOT-V1-PED-01 cites a monitoring claim scoped to admitted infants for an emergency-department vignette. Not load-bearing; the key is carried by the CPS management claim including its explicit sub-90% oxygen threshold.
